scope: Two final deterministic fallback PNGs, each actually viewed at original resolution. Proposed bilingual goals and all prompts read; final renderer read completely and SVG labels/geometry inspected. No generation/import/canonical edits made by this reviewer.
reviewMethod: Fresh visual inspection of final PNGs plus independently recalculated formulas, source/geometry checks and read-only renderer --check. The earlier Nano findings were already finalized. Native numerical checks are additional evidence, not a substitute for visual review.

nativeCheck.scope: Deterministic SVG source identity and mathematical assertions only.

checks: Twelve equal-width apertures at regular 28-unit centre intervals are visibly present. The g dimension joins the centres at SVG y=416 and 444, not the edges or a slit width.
The illumination arrows are parallel and normal to the aperture plane. Dashed lines are explicitly geometric references, so the midpoint in an opaque bar is not depicted as a spurious light source.
O=(880,430), P=(880,267.3346994592885), and the upper endpoint of the y1 dimension use the same height; the negative-order marker is at the symmetric y=592.6653005407115.
The angle arc has its actual centre at the shared aperture reference (250,430). The horizontal L dimension spans x=250 to 880, matching the screen plane and y=L tan(theta).
All formula cards and explanatory labels are legible, unobstructed and scientifically consistent: g sin(theta_m)=m lambda, integral orders, equal adjacent phase and far-field path difference.
The figure explicitly shows principal-maximum directions only and disclaims a scale-accurate intensity representation. It neither invents grating minima nor denies secondary maxima.
500 lines/mm means g=2 micrometres. Independently calculated sin(theta1)=0.25, theta1=14.477512185929923 degrees and y1=0.2581988897471611 m support all displayed rounded numbers.
The possible-order inequality includes grazing directions; the separate equality note correctly excludes their intersection with a finite screen.
Exactly one aperture is visible. Its width b runs edge-to-edge from SVG y=386 to 474. Normal parallel incident arrows and the stated uniform illumination/far-field model are consistent.

The common geometric origin is the aperture midpoint (250,430), O is (880,430), and the first positive minimum is (880,330). The opposite minimum is at y=530; y1 measures 430 to 330 and W measures 330 to 530.

The flat screen, horizontal L dimension, angle arc and geometric leg refer to the same planes and origin. The explicitly enlarged sketch angle is not falsely presented as the numerical example's tiny angle.

The bright centre, dark first minima and weak side bands have the right interpretation. The transverse raster intensity is computed using sin(atan(y/L)), normalized to the first minimum, not a silently linear y approximation.
The linear intensity graph defines I/I0 relative to the centre, uses u=b sin(theta)/lambda, has exactly one equally spaced tick at each -2,-1,0,+1,+2, stays nonnegative and is symmetric.

The actual sinc-squared plot has central height 1 and zeros exactly at nonzero integer u. Its first side peak at u=1.4302966531242027 has height 0.04719044922581128. In SVG coordinates the central rise is 163 and the side rise is 7.69204322380724, giving that same ratio; the orange pointer lands on the true side peak.
The visible side lobes are not artificially magnified and their labels do not sit on the half-order or zero ticks. The approximation warning is consistent with the plotted curve.
The minimum rule excludes m=0; the bright-centre note is explicit. Pairing corresponding points of the two half-apertures at the first minimum gives path difference lambda/2 and cancellation.

The example independently yields first minima ±5.000015625073242 mm, central width 10.000031250146485 mm and first secondary maxima ±7.151528985235306 mm; the displayed ±5.0, 10.0 and ±7.15 mm values are correct.
All symbols, labels and formula cards are readable. The W background patch and relocated theta label prevent line-through-text ambiguity without altering geometric endpoints.
